# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1223
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1223
- **Title**: gh-1219 compact: preserve epistemic status of claims — compaction keeps assertions but drops the evidence/uncertainty that would falsify them
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1219` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +73
- **Deletions**: -7
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T07:44:23Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T10:22:49Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

Compaction checkpoints were truth-neutral: the summarizer prompts said "Preserve EVERY fact" but had no rule keeping an uncertainty qualifier attached to its claim, no provenance tagging, and no evidence requirement for kept conclusions. A hedge like "machine review **may not** auto-approve" and its rule context competed for tokens on equal footing with hard facts, so a compacted agent could inherit the conclusion, lose the qualifier and evidence, and repeat the assumption as fact across every later turn. The loss happens entirely at summarization time — `summary_sanitizer.dart` never strips hedges — so the fix is the prompt contract itself.

### Fix

- `prompts/compaction/summary_system.md`: added the canonical epistemic-status rule — uncertainty qualifiers ("may", "suspect", "unconfirmed") stay verbatim with their claims (never detach/upgrade); claims are tagged `[verified]` / `[assumed]` / `[hearsay: source]` by how they are known; every kept conclusion carries one line of its why or the marker `unverified — re-verify` (the ticket's direction-3 re-verify queue, delivered inline in the checkpoint re-read every turn). The system prompt rides every summarization call: classic first summary, update fold, turn prefix, and the structured engine's checkpoint pass.
- `prompts/compaction/branch_summary.md`: handover digests now separate `## Observed State` (witnessed, with what produced it) from `## Interpreted State` (each inference names its observation; no observation = `unverified — re-verify`) — direction 4; unevidenced claims are never laundered into Observed State.
- `prompts/compaction/structured_checkpoint.md`, `turn_prefix.md`: same hedge/evidence rules on the instruction tails.
- `prompts/compaction/summary_update.md`: one budget-fitting rule — "PRESERVE provenance tags and hedges verbatim — never upgrade a hedge".
- `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart`: regenerated.

Constraint honored: issue #81 AC7 pins the net instruction delta of `summary.md` + `summary_update.md` at ≤500 chars, with only 77 chars of headroom left — the full contract therefore lives in the system prompt, not the budgeted task-prompt bodies.

### Test Coverage

- `test/compaction/compaction_test.dart`: 5 new pins — the epistemic contract on the system prompt (hedges, `[verified]`/`[assumed]`/`[hearsay]`, `unverified — re-verify`), the update-fold never-upgrade rule, turn-prefix hedges, structured-checkpoint evidence rule, and Observed/Interpreted separation in branch summaries. All failed before the prompt change (RED), pass after.
- `test/compaction/summary_sanitizer_test.dart`: hedge-survival pin — the pipeline's only mechanical strip point never rewrites "may not auto-approve", `[assumed]`, or "unconfirmed".
- AC7 budget test (`net instruction delta`): 494 ≤ 500 on the committed state.
- All 291 compaction/prompts tests pass. Full `dart test`: the only failures are pre-existing environment issues, verified byte-identical at the base commit — browser-ext e2e needs Chrome (dedicated CI workflow per `dart_test.yaml`), the PTY process-spawn integration tests and the `chatgpt_oauth` socket-bind test fail/skip under this sandbox's concurrency limits, and the trailing `tcache` abort (EXIT=134) is the documented PTY-native teardown race (`test/integration/zz_probe_test.dart`, 2026-10-03).

### Notes

- Direction 3's standalone "re-verify queue on resume" surface is covered minimally: the `unverified — re-verify` marker lands in the checkpoint text the agent re-reads every turn; a dedicated mechanical queue (session records driving a resume notice) is a larger feature, intentionally out of scope for this fix.
- No code-path changes — summary shape, sanitization, and projection are untouched; prompts only. Users with `prompts:` overrides of these files keep their overrides (this changes only the built-ins).

    "description": "### Root Cause

Compaction checkpoints were truth-neutral: the summarizer prompts said "Preserve EVERY fact" but had no rule keeping an uncertainty qualifier attached to its claim, no provenance tagging, and no evidence requirement for kept conclusions. A hedge like "machine review **may not** auto-approve" and its rule context competed for tokens on equal footing with hard facts, so a compacted agent could inherit the conclusion, lose the qualifier and evidence, and repeat the assumption as fact across every later turn. The loss happens entirely at summarization time — `summary_sanitizer.dart` never strips hedges — so the fix is the prompt contract itself.

### Fix

- `prompts/compaction/summary_system.md`: added the canonical epistemic-status rule — uncertainty qualifiers ("may", "suspect", "unconfirmed") stay verbatim with their claims (never detach/upgrade); claims are tagged `[verified]` / `[assumed]` / `[hearsay: source]` by how they are known; every kept conclusion carries one line of its why or the marker `unverified — re-verify` (the ticket's direction-3 re-verify queue, delivered inline in the checkpoint re-read every turn). The system prompt rides every summarization call: classic first summary, update fold, turn prefix, and the structured engine's checkpoint pass.
- `prompts/compaction/branch_summary.md`: handover digests now separate `## Observed State` (witnessed, with what produced it) from `## Interpreted State` (each inference names its observation; no observation = `unverified — re-verify`) — direction 4; unevidenced claims are never laundered into Observed State.
- `prompts/compaction/structured_checkpoint.md`, `turn_prefix.md`: same hedge/evidence rules on the instruction tails.
- `prompts/compaction/summary_update.md`: one budget-fitting rule — "PRESERVE provenance tags and hedges verbatim — never upgrade a hedge".
- `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart`: regenerated.

Constraint honored: issue #81 AC7 pins the net instruction delta of `summary.md` + `summary_update.md` at ≤500 chars, with only 77 chars of headroom left — the full contract therefore lives in the system prompt, not the budgeted task-prompt bodies.

### Test Coverage

- `test/compaction/compaction_test.dart`: 5 new pins — the epistemic contract on the system prompt (hedges, `[verified]`/`[assumed]`/`[hearsay]`, `unverified — re-verify`), the update-fold never-upgrade rule, turn-prefix hedges, structured-checkpoint evidence rule, and Observed/Interpreted separation in branch summaries. All failed before the prompt change (RED), pass after.
- `test/compaction/summary_sanitizer_test.dart`: hedge-survival pin — the pipeline's only mechanical strip point never rewrites "may not auto-approve", `[assumed]`, or "unconfirmed".
- AC7 budget test (`net instruction delta`): 494 ≤ 500 on the committed state.
- All 291 compaction/prompts tests pass. - Direction 3's standalone "re-verify queue on resume" surface is covered minimally: the `unverified — re-verify` marker lands in the checkpoint text the agent re-reads every turn; a dedicated mechanical queue (session records driving a resume notice) is a larger feature, intentionally out of scope for this fix.

So the turn_prefix body omission is fine (defense in depth on the body is uneven but not a bug). Not worth flagging beyond a SUGGESTION? Hmm. 3. **Branch summary doesn't get the system prompt**: generateBranchSummary → summarize(SummarizationRequest(prompt: ...)). 7. **Scope**: matches ticket gh-1219. The PR is prompts-only; no code changes. Backward compat: users with prompt overrides keep theirs (overrides resolve by id; new built-in text only applies when not overridden). No migration issues.

8. Potential issue: **`## Observed State` / `## Interpreted State` in branch_summary.md vs downstream consumers** — no Dart parser for these sections (verified: no "Observed" in lib/ outside prompts.g.dart). The summary is free text in a branch_summary record. Safe.

That's inherent to the prompt-architecture (each call path must carry its rules since system prompt may be overridden independently? No — system prompt + body both come from the same bundle; overrides resolve per-id). The duplication is deliberate (bodies must be self-contained because users can override individual files). Not a finding; the PR description explains the budget constraint.

# Changelog

## 1.0.485


- fix(ci): Daily auto-publish `pub.dev` leg — poll the pub.dev API until it
  reflects the rerun's publish instead of a single read. 2026-09-28: the
  recovery rerun published AND self-verified 1.0.483 (`pub.dev verified`
  at 05:44:11Z), but the leg's one-shot API query 52s later hit a stale
  replica, saw 1.0.482 and false-errored "manual publish needed". Initial
  behind-check now takes three spaced reads (newest wins) so a stale read
  cannot trigger unnecessary recovery either.
- fix(ci): `install-pin-bump` no longer hard-gates on `release-provenance`.
  When provenance FAILED (binaries/signature upload race), the marker job
  was left SKIPPED — and `rerun --failed` never resurrects skipped jobs, so
  the `vpinned` marker stayed stale forever (v1.0.483: the recovery rerun
  went green, the marker never advanced). The job now uses
  `if: always()`; `pin_release.sh`'s own pre-move provenance gate
  (`check_install_pin.sh` with `FA_PIN_TARGET`) fails it loudly instead of
  moving the marker, and a FAILED job IS part of `rerun --failed` — so the
  recovery cascade reaches it.

## 1.0.483


- fix(install): the pinned default is now the `vpinned` RELEASE MARKER —
  no committed pin at all. `install-config.yaml` `pinned_cli_version`
  said 0.1.452 while the generated `site/install.sh` carried 1.0.480
  (#1015 hand-edited only the generated file): a committed pin rots, and a
  pin advanced by committing/pushing from the release pipeline re-races
  `auto_release` and re-triggers Pages on every tag. Instead, the
  installer resolves the standing `vpinned` release marker (its
  `PINNED_VERSION` asset names the known-good release) and verifies the
  pointed release exactly as before — the marker is only a pointer, so a
  tampered one fails closed (DoS at worst, never a bad binary; the
  embedded trust anchor stays the real trust root).
  `scripts/pin_release.sh` advances the marker from the tag-scoped
  `install-pin-bump` CI job after `release-provenance` signs the release:

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1223
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1223
- **Title**: gh-1219 compact: preserve epistemic status of claims — compaction keeps assertions but drops the evidence/uncertainty that would falsify them
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1219` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +73
- **Deletions**: -7
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T07:44:23Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T10:22:49Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

Compaction checkpoints were truth-neutral: the summarizer prompts said "Preserve EVERY fact" but had no rule keeping an uncertainty qualifier attached to its claim, no provenance tagging, and no evidence requirement for kept conclusions. A hedge like "machine review **may not** auto-approve" and its rule context competed for tokens on equal footing with hard facts, so a compacted agent could inherit the conclusion, lose the qualifier and evidence, and repeat the assumption as fact across every later turn. The loss happens entirely at summarization time — `summary_sanitizer.dart` never strips hedges — so the fix is the prompt contract itself.

### Fix

- `prompts/compaction/summary_system.md`: added the canonical epistemic-status rule — uncertainty qualifiers ("may", "suspect", "unconfirmed") stay verbatim with their claims (never detach/upgrade); claims are tagged `[verified]` / `[assumed]` / `[hearsay: source]` by how they are known; every kept conclusion carries one line of its why or the marker `unverified — re-verify` (the ticket's direction-3 re-verify queue, delivered inline in the checkpoint re-read every turn). The system prompt rides every summarization call: classic first summary, update fold, turn prefix, and the structured engine's checkpoint pass.
- `prompts/compaction/branch_summary.md`: handover digests now separate `## Observed State` (witnessed, with what produced it) from `## Interpreted State` (each inference names its observation; no observation = `unverified — re-verify`) — direction 4; unevidenced claims are never laundered into Observed State.
- `prompts/compaction/structured_checkpoint.md`, `turn_prefix.md`: same hedge/evidence rules on the instruction tails.
- `prompts/compaction/summary_update.md`: one budget-fitting rule — "PRESERVE provenance tags and hedges verbatim — never upgrade a hedge".
- `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart`: regenerated.

Constraint honored: issue #81 AC7 pins the net instruction delta of `summary.md` + `summary_update.md` at ≤500 chars, with only 77 chars of headroom left — the full contract therefore lives in the system prompt, not the budgeted task-prompt bodies.

### Test Coverage

- `test/compaction/compaction_test.dart`: 5 new pins — the epistemic contract on the system prompt (hedges, `[verified]`/`[assumed]`/`[hearsay]`, `unverified — re-verify`), the update-fold never-upgrade rule, turn-prefix hedges, structured-checkpoint evidence rule, and Observed/Interpreted separation in branch summaries. All failed before the prompt change (RED), pass after.
- `test/compaction/summary_sanitizer_test.dart`: hedge-survival pin — the pipeline's only mechanical strip point never rewrites "may not auto-approve", `[assumed]`, or "unconfirmed".
- AC7 budget test (`net instruction delta`): 494 ≤ 500 on the committed state.
- All 291 compaction/prompts tests pass. Full `dart test`: the only failures are pre-existing environment issues, verified byte-identical at the base commit — browser-ext e2e needs Chrome (dedicated CI workflow per `dart_test.yaml`), the PTY process-spawn integration tests and the `chatgpt_oauth` socket-bind test fail/skip under this sandbox's concurrency limits, and the trailing `tcache` abort (EXIT=134) is the documented PTY-native teardown race (`test/integration/zz_probe_test.dart`, 2026-10-03).

### Notes

- Direction 3's standalone "re-verify queue on resume" surface is covered minimally: the `unverified — re-verify` marker lands in the checkpoint text the agent re-reads every turn; a dedicated mechanical queue (session records driving a resume notice) is a larger feature, intentionally out of scope for this fix.
- No code-path changes — summary shape, sanitization, and projection are untouched; prompts only. Users with `prompts:` overrides of these files keep their overrides (this changes only the built-ins).

  "fields": {
    "summary": "gh-1219 compact: preserve epistemic status of claims — compaction keeps assertions but drops the evidence/uncertainty that would falsify them",
    "description": "### Root Cause

Compaction checkpoints were truth-neutral: the summarizer prompts said "Preserve EVERY fact" but had no rule keeping an uncertainty qualifier attached to its claim, no provenance tagging, and no evidence requirement for kept conclusions. A hedge like "machine review **may not** auto-approve" and its rule context competed for tokens on equal footing with hard facts, so a compacted agent could inherit the conclusion, lose the qualifier and evidence, and repeat the assumption as fact across every later turn. The loss happens entirely at summarization time — `summary_sanitizer.dart` never strips hedges — so the fix is the prompt contract itself.

### Fix

- `prompts/compaction/summary_system.md`: added the canonical epistemic-status rule — uncertainty qualifiers ("may", "suspect", "unconfirmed") stay verbatim with their claims (never detach/upgrade); claims are tagged `[verified]` / `[assumed]` / `[hearsay: source]` by how they are known; every kept conclusion carries one line of its why or the marker `unverified — re-verify` (the ticket's direction-3 re-verify queue, delivered inline in the checkpoint re-read every turn). The system prompt rides every summarization call: classic first summary, update fold, turn prefix, and the structured engine's checkpoint pass.
- `prompts/compaction/branch_summary.md`: handover digests now separate `## Observed State` (witnessed, with what produced it) from `## Interpreted State` (each inference names its observation; no observation = `unverified — re-verify`) — direction 4; unevidenced claims are never laundered into Observed State.
- `prompts/compaction/structured_checkpoint.md`, `turn_prefix.md`: same hedge/evidence rules on the instruction tails.
- `prompts/compaction/summary_update.md`: one budget-fitting rule — "PRESERVE provenance tags and hedges verbatim — never upgrade a hedge".
- `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart`: regenerated.

Constraint honored: issue #81 AC7 pins the net instruction delta of `summary.md` + `summary_update.md` at ≤500 chars, with only 77 chars of headroom left — the full contract therefore lives in the system prompt, not the budgeted task-prompt bodies.

### Test Coverage

- `test/compaction/compaction_test.dart`: 5 new pins — the epistemic contract on the system prompt (hedges, `[verified]`/`[assumed]`/`[hearsay]`, `unverified — re-verify`), the update-fold never-upgrade rule, turn-prefix hedges, structured-checkpoint evidence rule, and Observed/Interpreted separation in branch summaries. All failed before the prompt change (RED), pass after.
- `test/compaction/summary_sanitizer_test.dart`: hedge-survival pin — the pipeline's only mechanical strip point never rewrites "may not auto-approve", `[assumed]`, or "unconfirmed".
- AC7 budget test (`net instruction delta`): 494 ≤ 500 on the committed state.
- All 291 compaction/prompts tests pass. Full `dart test`: the only failures are pre-existing environment issues, verified byte-identical at the base commit — browser-ext e2e needs Chrome (dedicated CI workflow per `dart_test.yaml`), the PTY process-spawn integration tests and the `chatgpt_oauth` socket-bind test fail/skip under this sandbox's concurrency limits, and the trailing `tcache` abort (EXIT=134) is the documented PTY-native teardown race (`test/integration/zz_probe_test.dart`, 2026-10-03).

### Notes

- Direction 3's standalone "re-verify queue on resume" surface is covered minimally: the `unverified — re-verify` marker lands in the checkpoint text the agent re-reads every turn; a dedicated mechanical queue (session records driving a resume notice) is a larger feature, intentionally out of scope for this fix.
- No code-path changes — summary shape, sanitization, and projection are untouched; prompts only. Users with `prompts:` overrides of these files keep their overrides (this changes only the built-ins)."

# Changelog

## 1.0.485


- fix(ci): Daily auto-publish `pub.dev` leg — poll the pub.dev API until it
  reflects the rerun's publish instead of a single read. 2026-09-28: the
  recovery rerun published AND self-verified 1.0.483 (`pub.dev verified`
  at 05:44:11Z), but the leg's one-shot API query 52s later hit a stale
  replica, saw 1.0.482 and false-errored "manual publish needed". Initial
  behind-check now takes three spaced reads (newest wins) so a stale read
  cannot trigger unnecessary recovery either.
- fix(ci): `install-pin-bump` no longer hard-gates on `release-provenance`.
  When provenance FAILED (binaries/signature upload race), the marker job
  was left SKIPPED — and `rerun --failed` never resurrects skipped jobs, so
  the `vpinned` marker stayed stale forever (v1.0.483: the recovery rerun
  went green, the marker never advanced). The job now uses
  `if: always()`; `pin_release.sh`'s own pre-move provenance gate
  (`check_install_pin.sh` with `FA_PIN_TARGET`) fails it loudly instead of
  moving the marker, and a FAILED job IS part of `rerun --failed` — so the
  recovery cascade reaches it.

## 1.0.483


- fix(install): the pinned default is now the `vpinned` RELEASE MARKER —
  no committed pin at all. `install-config.yaml` `pinned_cli_version`
  said 0.1.452 while the generated `site/install.sh` carried 1.0.480
  (#1015 hand-edited only the generated file): a committed pin rots, and a
  pin advanced by committing/pushing from the release pipeline re-races
  `auto_release` and re-triggers Pages on every tag. Instead, the
  installer resolves the standing `vpinned` release marker (its
  `PINNED_VERSION` asset names the known-good release) and verifies the
  pointed release exactly as before — the marker is only a pointer, so a
  tampered one fails closed (DoS at worst, never a bad binary; the
  embedded trust anchor stays the real trust root).
  `scripts/pin_release.sh` advances the marker from the tag-scoped
  `install-pin-bump` CI job after `release-provenance` signs the release:

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1223
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1223
- **Title**: gh-1219 compact: preserve epistemic status of claims — compaction keeps assertions but drops the evidence/uncertainty that would falsify them
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1219` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +73
- **Deletions**: -7
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T07:44:23Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T10:22:49Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

Compaction checkpoints were truth-neutral: the summarizer prompts said "Preserve EVERY fact" but had no rule keeping an uncertainty qualifier attached to its claim, no provenance tagging, and no evidence requirement for kept conclusions. A hedge like "machine review **may not** auto-approve" and its rule context competed for tokens on equal footing with hard facts, so a compacted agent could inherit the conclusion, lose the qualifier and evidence, and repeat the assumption as fact across every later turn. The loss happens entirely at summarization time — `summary_sanitizer.dart` never strips hedges — so the fix is the prompt contract itself.

### Fix

- `prompts/compaction/summary_system.md`: added the canonical epistemic-status rule — uncertainty qualifiers ("may", "suspect", "unconfirmed") stay verbatim with their claims (never detach/upgrade); claims are tagged `[verified]` / `[assumed]` / `[hearsay: source]` by how they are known; every kept conclusion carries one line of its why or the marker `unverified — re-verify` (the ticket's direction-3 re-verify queue, delivered inline in the checkpoint re-read every turn). The system prompt rides every summarization call: classic first summary, update fold, turn prefix, and the structured engine's checkpoint pass.
- `prompts/compaction/branch_summary.md`: handover digests now separate `## Observed State` (witnessed, with what produced it) from `## Interpreted State` (each inference names its observation; no observation = `unverified — re-verify`) — direction 4; unevidenced claims are never laundered into Observed State.
- `prompts/compaction/structured_checkpoint.md`, `turn_prefix.md`: same hedge/evidence rules on the instruction tails.
- `prompts/compaction/summary_update.md`: one budget-fitting rule — "PRESERVE provenance tags and hedges verbatim — never upgrade a hedge".
- `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart`: regenerated.

Constraint honored: issue #81 AC7 pins the net instruction delta of `summary.md` + `summary_update.md` at ≤500 chars, with only 77 chars of headroom left — the full contract therefore lives in the system prompt, not the budgeted task-prompt bodies.

### Test Coverage

# pr-1223: gh-1219 compact: preserve epistemic status of claims — compaction keeps assertions but drops the evidence/uncertainty that would falsify them

## Description

### Root Cause

Compaction checkpoints were truth-neutral: the summarizer prompts said "Preserve EVERY fact" but had no rule keeping an uncertainty qualifier attached to its claim, no provenance tagging, and no evidence requirement for kept conclusions. A hedge like "machine review **may not** auto-approve" and its rule context competed for tokens on equal footing with hard facts, so a compacted agent could inherit the conclusion, lose the qualifier and evidence, and repeat the assumption as fact across every later turn. The loss happens entirely at summarization time — `summary_sanitizer.dart` never strips hedges — so the fix is the prompt contract itself.

### Fix

- `prompts/compaction/summary_system.md`: added the canonical epistemic-status rule — uncertainty qualifiers ("may", "suspect", "unconfirmed") stay verbatim with their claims (never detach/upgrade); claims are tagged `[verified]` / `[assumed]` / `[hearsay: source]` by how they are known; every kept conclusion carries one line of its why or the marker `unverified — re-verify` (the ticket's direction-3 re-verify queue, delivered inline in the checkpoint re-read every turn). The system prompt rides every summarization call: classic first summary, update fold, turn prefix, and the structured engine's checkpoint pass.
- `prompts/compaction/branch_summary.md`: handover digests now separate `## Observed State` (witnessed, with what produced it) from `## Interpreted State` (each inference names its observation; no observation = `unverified — re-verify`) — direction 4; unevidenced claims are never laundered into Observed State.
- `prompts/compaction/structured_checkpoint.md`, `turn_prefix.md`: same hedge/evidence rules on the instruction tails.
- `prompts/compaction/summary_update.md`: one budget-fitting rule — "PRESERVE provenance tags and hedges verbatim — never upgrade a hedge".
- `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart`: regenerated.

Constraint honored: issue #81 AC7 pins the net instruction delta of `summary.md` + `summary_update.md` at ≤500 chars, with only 77 chars of headroom left — the full contract therefore lives in the system prompt, not the budgeted task-prompt bodies.

### Test Coverage

- `test/compaction/compaction_test.dart`: 5 new pins — the epistemic contract on the system prompt (hedges, `[verified]`/`[assumed]`/`[hearsay]`, `unverified — re-verify`), the update-fold never-upgrade rule, turn-prefix hedges, structured-checkpoint evidence rule, and Observed/Interpreted separation in branch summaries. - AC7 budget test (`net instruction delta`): 494 ≤ 500 on the committed state.
- All 291 compaction/prompts tests pass. # Changelog

## 1.0.485


- fix(ci): Daily auto-publish `pub.dev` leg — poll the pub.dev API until it
  reflects the rerun's publish instead of a single read. 2026-09-28: the
  recovery rerun published AND self-verified 1.0.483 (`pub.dev verified`
  at 05:44:11Z), but the leg's one-shot API query 52s later hit a stale
  replica, saw 1.0.482 and false-errored "manual publish needed". Initial
  behind-check now takes three spaced reads (newest wins) so a stale read
  cannot trigger unnecessary recovery either.
- fix(ci): `install-pin-bump` no longer hard-gates on `release-provenance`.
  When provenance FAILED (binaries/signature upload race), the marker job
  was left SKIPPED — and `rerun --failed` never resurrects skipped jobs, so
  the `vpinned` marker stayed stale forever (v1.0.483: the recovery rerun
  went green, the marker never advanced). The job now uses
  `if: always()`; `pin_release.sh`'s own pre-move provenance gate
  (`check_install_pin.sh` with `FA_PIN_TARGET`) fails it loudly instead of
  moving the marker, and a FAILED job IS part of `rerun --failed` — so the
  recovery cascade reaches it.

## 1.0.483


- fix(install): the pinned default is now the `vpinned` RELEASE MARKER —
  no committed pin at all. `install-config.yaml` `pinned_cli_version`
  said 0.1.452 while the generated `site/install.sh` carried 1.0.480
  (#1015 hand-edited only the generated file): a committed pin rots, and a
  pin advanced by committing/pushing from the release pipeline re-races

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1223
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1223
- **Title**: gh-1219 compact: preserve epistemic status of claims — compaction keeps assertions but drops the evidence/uncertainty that would falsify them
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1219` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +73
- **Deletions**: -7
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T07:44:23Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T10:22:49Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

Compaction checkpoints were truth-neutral: the summarizer prompts said "Preserve EVERY fact" but had no rule keeping an uncertainty qualifier attached to its claim, no provenance tagging, and no evidence requirement for kept conclusions. A hedge like "machine review **may not** auto-approve" and its rule context competed for tokens on equal footing with hard facts, so a compacted agent could inherit the conclusion, lose the qualifier and evidence, and repeat the assumption as fact across every later turn. The loss happens entirely at summarization time — `summary_sanitizer.dart` never strips hedges — so the fix is the prompt contract itself.

### Fix

- `prompts/compaction/summary_system.md`: added the canonical epistemic-status rule — uncertainty qualifiers ("may", "suspect", "unconfirmed") stay verbatim with their claims (never detach/upgrade); claims are tagged `[verified]` / `[assumed]` / `[hearsay: source]` by how they are known; every kept conclusion carries one line of its why or the marker `unverified — re-verify` (the ticket's direction-3 re-verify queue, delivered inline in the checkpoint re-read every turn). The system prompt rides every summarization call: classic first summary, update fold, turn prefix, and the structured engine's checkpoint pass.
- `prompts/compaction/branch_summary.md`: handover digests now separate `## Observed State` (witnessed, with what produced it) from `## Interpreted State` (each inference names its observation; no observation = `unverified — re-verify`) — direction 4; unevidenced claims are never laundered into Observed State.
- `prompts/compaction/structured_checkpoint.md`, `turn_prefix.md`: same hedge/evidence rules on the instruction tails.
- `prompts/compaction/summary_update.md`: one budget-fitting rule — "PRESERVE provenance tags and hedges verbatim — never upgrade a hedge".
- `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart`: regenerated.

Constraint honored: issue #81 AC7 pins the net instruction delta of `summary.md` + `summary_update.md` at ≤500 chars, with only 77 chars of headroom left — the full contract therefore lives in the system prompt, not the budgeted task-prompt bodies.

### Test Coverage

- `test/compaction/compaction_test.dart`: 5 new pins — the epistemic contract on the system prompt (hedges, `[verified]`/`[assumed]`/`[hearsay]`, `unverified — re-verify`), the update-fold never-upgrade rule, turn-prefix hedges, structured-checkpoint evidence rule, and Observed/Interpreted separation in branch summaries. All failed before the prompt change (RED), pass after.
- `test/compaction/summary_sanitizer_test.dart`: hedge-survival pin — the pipeline's only mechanical strip point never rewrites "may not auto-approve", `[assumed]`, or "unconfirmed".
- AC7 budget test (`net instruction delta`): 494 ≤ 500 on the committed state.
- All 291 compaction/prompts tests pass. Full `dart test`: the only failures are pre-existing environment issues, verified byte-identical at the base commit — browser-ext e2e needs Chrome (dedicated CI workflow per `dart_test.yaml`), the PTY process-spawn integration tests and the `chatgpt_oauth` socket-bind test fail/skip under this sandbox's concurrency limits, and the trailing `tcache` abort (EXIT=134) is the documented PTY-native teardown race (`test/integration/zz_probe_test.dart`, 2026-10-03).

### Notes

- Direction 3's standalone "re-verify queue on resume" surface is covered minimally: the `unverified — re-verify` marker lands in the checkpoint text the agent re-reads every turn; a dedicated mechanical queue (session records driving a resume notice) is a larger feature, intentionally out of scope for this fix.
- No code-path changes — summary shape, sanitization, and projection are untouched; prompts only. Users with `prompts:` overrides of these files keep their overrides (this changes only the built-ins).

# Changelog

## 1.0.485


- fix(ci): Daily auto-publish `pub.dev` leg — poll the pub.dev API until it
  reflects the rerun's publish instead of a single read. 2026-09-28: the
  recovery rerun published AND self-verified 1.0.483 (`pub.dev verified`
  at 05:44:11Z), but the leg's one-shot API query 52s later hit a stale
  replica, saw 1.0.482 and false-errored "manual publish needed". Initial
  behind-check now takes three spaced reads (newest wins) so a stale read
  cannot trigger unnecessary recovery either.
- fix(ci): `install-pin-bump` no longer hard-gates on `release-provenance`.
  When provenance FAILED (binaries/signature upload race), the marker job
  was left SKIPPED — and `rerun --failed` never resurrects skipped jobs, so
  the `vpinned` marker stayed stale forever (v1.0.483: the recovery rerun
  went green, the marker never advanced). The job now uses
  `if: always()`; `pin_release.sh`'s own pre-move provenance gate
  (`check_install_pin.sh` with `FA_PIN_TARGET`) fails it loudly instead of
  moving the marker, and a FAILED job IS part of `rerun --failed` — so the
  recovery cascade reaches it.

## 1.0.483


- fix(install): the pinned default is now the `vpinned` RELEASE MARKER —
  no committed pin at all. `install-config.yaml` `pinned_cli_version`
  said 0.1.452 while the generated `site/install.sh` carried 1.0.480
  (#1015 hand-edited only the generated file): a committed pin rots, and a
  pin advanced by committing/pushing from the release pipeline re-races
  `auto_release` and re-triggers Pages on every tag. Instead, the
  installer resolves the standing `vpinned` release marker (its
  `PINNED_VERSION` asset names the known-good release) and verifies the
  pointed release exactly as before — the marker is only a pointer, so a
  tampered one fails closed (DoS at worst, never a bad binary; the
  embedded trust anchor stays the real trust root).
  `scripts/pin_release.sh` advances the marker from the tag-scoped
  `install-pin-bump` CI job after `release-provenance` signs the release:
